english.title: Part with possession of a section 1 firearm / ammunition to a person under 14 years of age
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) parted with the possession of

(A)_[a firearm]_
(B)_[ammunition]_

namely **(..SPECIFY TYPE..) to which section 1 of the Firearms Act 1968 applied to **(..SPECIFY NAME..) a person under the age of 14
english.legislation: Contrary to section 24(2) of and Schedule 6 to the Firearms Act 1968.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
parted with the possession of a section 1 firearm/ammunition
to a person under the age of fourteen years

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) The exceptions to 'parting with possession' are contained in s.11(1), (3) And (4) of the Act, relating to sports, athletics and other approved activities or section 15 of the Firearms Amendment Act 1988.
(ii) See also offence wordings H512 and H573.

other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
48 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
